FFmpeg 7.1.5 — "export-ass-zimg" LGPL static build for Windows x64, plus ffprobe (decode)
STATUS: BUILT AND VERIFIED LOCALLY, NOT APPROVED. The digests below are from a local validation
build on 2026-10-11 (Dell, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300). The catalog binary is to come from the
GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/ffmpeg-windows.yml, which has not run yet; its
toolchain packages may differ in version, so its digest may differ from the one below.

Purpose: CutRight (and GenRight) export on Windows through rightkit-media VerifiedFfmpeg, with
the same library set as the macOS export-ass-zimg variant:
  - libass `subtitles` / `ass` filters (system fonts through DirectWrite)
  - FreeType + HarfBuzz `drawtext`, FriBidi
  - zimg `zscale` (HDR and log to Rec.709 with `tonemap`)
  - zlib (PNG), Media Foundation encoders (h264_mf, hevc_mf, aac_mf), built-in AAC encoder
keeping the catalog's LGPL-only, no-autodetect posture.

Recipe: crates/rightkit-media/recipes/build-ffmpeg-windows.sh (pinned sources in
        recipes/ffmpeg-sources.json and recipes/ffmpeg-sources-windows.json; the build refuses
        unpinned or mismatched sources).

FFmpeg configure (exact, as built):
  --disable-gpl --disable-nonfree --disable-autodetect --enable-static --disable-shared
  --disable-doc --disable-debug --disable-ffplay --enable-small --arch=x86_64
  --target-os=mingw32 --enable-libass --enable-libfreetype --enable-libharfbuzz
  --enable-libzimg --enable-zlib --enable-mediafoundation --pkg-config-flags=--static
  --extra-ldflags='-static -static-libgcc -Wl,--no-insert-timestamp'
ffprobe (decode variant) is the approved Windows decode line (BUILD-NOTES.txt) plus
  -Wl,--no-insert-timestamp, built with `make ffprobe.exe`:
  --disable-gpl --disable-nonfree --disable-autodetect --enable-static --disable-shared
  --disable-doc --disable-debug --disable-ffplay --enable-small --arch=x86_64
  --target-os=mingw32 --extra-ldflags='-static -static-libgcc -Wl,--no-insert-timestamp'
Include and library paths come only from the private prefix's .pc files, so the embedded
configuration string holds no build-host path (`strings` finds no work-directory path in the
exe). pkg-config is confined to the prefix (PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR and PKG_CONFIG_PATH both point
at <prefix>/lib/pkgconfig).

Dependency builds (static, into the private prefix, CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS -O2):
  zlib 1.3.2       win32/Makefile.gcc, target libz.a only (no zlib1.dll); headers, libz.a and a
                   generated zlib.pc are copied into the prefix
  FreeType 2.13.3  autotools  --without-zlib --without-bzip2 --without-png --without-harfbuzz
                              --without-brotli
  FriBidi 1.0.16   meson      -Ddocs=false -Dbin=false -Dtests=false -Ddeprecated=true; built only
                              from files present in the upstream git tag (same deletion list as
                              the macOS recipe; tables regenerated by host-built generators)
  HarfBuzz 10.1.0  meson      -Dfreetype=enabled; glib, gobject, cairo, icu, graphite, graphite2,
                              coretext, gdi, directwrite, chafa, wasm, tests, docs, utilities,
                              introspection, benchmark disabled
  libass 0.17.3    autotools  --disable-fontconfig --enable-directwrite
                              --disable-require-system-font-provider ac_cv_header_iconv_h=no
                              (keeps MSYS2's own libiconv out; the recipe fails if config.h
                              defines CONFIG_ICONV or lacks CONFIG_DIRECTWRITE)
  zimg 3.0.5       autotools  autoreconf --install --force (the tag archive has no configure),
                              then the default configuration
All autotools builds: --host=x86_64-w64-mingw32 --build=x86_64-w64-mingw32 --disable-shared
--enable-static. meson uses a native file naming gcc, g++, ar, strip and the native pkg-config.

Tool versions (local validation build):
  MSYS2 MINGW64 shell (msvcrt runtime), started with a clean environment
  mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc 16.1.0-5 (gcc 16.1.0 Rev5), binutils 2.46.1-1, crt/headers/winpthreads
    14.0.0.r98.g19f5121a2-1
  NASM 2.16.03, GNU Make 4.4.1, autoconf 2.73, automake 1.18.1, libtool 2.5.4
  meson 1.12.1, ninja 1.13.2 (reports 1.13.2.git.kitware.jobserver-pipe-1), pkgconf 3.0.7
    (PyPI wheels meson, ninja, pkgconf 3.0.7.post0 in a throwaway venv, Python 3.10.11; passed
    to the recipe as MESON, NINJA, PKG_CONFIG, PYTHON). MSYS2's own /usr/bin/pkgconf is not
    used: it is an MSYS program and gives meson POSIX paths.
  Installed into C:\msys64 for this build: autoconf, automake, libtool (pacman).

    the pins and upstream evidence in recipes/ffmpeg-sources.json (see
    BUILD-NOTES-ffmpeg-export-ass-macos.txt and BUILD-NOTES-ffmpeg-export-ass-zimg-macos.txt).
    All six digests were re-observed on the Windows host and match.
  zlib-1.3.2.tar.xz
    d7a0654783a4da529d1bb793b7ad9c3318020af77667bcae35f95d0e42a792f3
    https://zlib.net/zlib-1.3.2.tar.xz
    https://zlib.net/ (fetched 2026-10-11) lists exactly this SHA-256: signature not checked,
    digest matched publisher (accepted; the Windows host has no gpg for zlib-1.3.2.tar.xz.asc).
  zimg 3.0.5 (GitHub archive of tag release-3.0.5)
    a9a0226bf85e0d83c41a8ebe4e3e690e1348682f6a2a7838f1b8cbff1b799bcf
    The Windows host observed the same digest as the shared pin, whose evidence records the
    file-by-file comparison with the tag. That comparison was not repeated on Windows.

Binaries (local validation build, D:\.dev-cache\rk-ffmpeg-win\out, outside the repository):
  ffmpeg-export-ass-windows-x64.exe   (built before the variant was renamed export-ass-zimg;
                                       same commands)
    sha256 ea97989ef797f472ead7a544fe53fa57f94c4b91cf2f7902dbeb684a6fb07b15, 19607552 bytes
  ffprobe-decode-windows-x64.exe
    sha256 1be036043af54835fa942b3dbd2d1c1bc362f235b5a5c85c8eeb4eb065937b55, 16307200 bytes
Each has <name>.evidence.json and <name>.evidence/ (configure-line, version, buildconf, L,
encoders, decoders, filters, imports) and <name>.notices/.
Reproducibility: NOT yet checked. Each was built once. -Wl,--no-insert-timestamp zeroes the PE
timestamp so two builds can be compared; the comparison is to be done with two CI runs.

Verification (both exes; gates enforced by the recipe)
  Imports (objdump -p), identical for both: AVICAP32, bcrypt, GDI32, KERNEL32, msvcrt, ole32,
    OLEAUT32, SHELL32, SHLWAPI, USER32, WS2_32 — all in %SystemRoot%\System32. No
    libwinpthread-1.dll, libgcc, libstdc++, msys-2.0.dll, libiconv or zlib1.dll.
  -version: "ffmpeg version 7.1.5", "built with gcc 16.1.0 (Rev5, Built by MSYS2 project)";
    -buildconf equals the configure line above.
  -L reports the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 or later. config.h:
    FFMPEG_LICENSE "LGPL version 2.1 or later", CONFIG_GPL 0, CONFIG_NONFREE 0,
    CONFIG_VERSION3 0, CONFIG_ICONV 0, HAVE_W32THREADS 1, HAVE_PTHREADS 0.
    No --enable-gpl, --enable-nonfree or --enable-version3 anywhere in the configuration.
  ffmpeg export build: 193 encoder lines, 506 decoder lines, 453 filter lines in the listings.
  Filters, all PRESENT: zscale, tonemap, overlay, loudnorm, drawtext, freezedetect, blackdetect,
    ebur128, silencedetect, lut3d, signalstats, astats, pad, colorspace, amix, tpad,
    colorbalance, colortemperature, lutrgb, lutyuv, adelay, transpose, highpass, alimiter,
    subtitles, ass, scale. ABSENT, as required: eq (eq_filter_deps="gpl").
    Colour conversion: zscale (zimg) and the native colorspace and scale filters all exist.
  Encoders present: h264_mf, hevc_mf, aac (built-in), aac_mf, ac3_mf, mp3_mf, png.
    Absent: libx264, libx265, libopenh264, h264_nvenc, h264_amf, h264_qsv.
  Smoke test on the build host (2 s, 320x240, 25 fps; frame at 1 s decoded to gray8):
    black + 440 Hz sine -> h264_mf + aac MP4: 0 bright (>128) pixels;
    `subtitles=t.ass` (Arial through DirectWrite): 1406 bright pixels in rows 150-239, 0 in
      rows 0-99; `drawtext=fontfile=C:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf`: 1322 and 0. The frames were
      inspected visually (legible "BURNED IN" / "CAPTION").
    testsrc2 tagged bt2020 / smpte2084 / bt2020nc, 10-bit ->
      zscale=t=linear:npl=100,format=gbrpf32le,zscale=p=bt709,tonemap=hable,
      zscale=t=bt709:m=bt709:r=tv,format=nv12 -> h264_mf: encodes; the output stream is
      tagged yuv420p(tv, bt709).

Encoder choices
  Included: Media Foundation (--enable-mediafoundation). It is a Windows system component, needs
    no extra source and no nonfree flag; the import table does not list the Media Foundation
    DLLs and h264_mf encoded in the smoke test above.
  Left out: nvenc, amf, qsv. Each needs a further third-party source (nv-codec-headers, the AMF
    headers, libvpl) that is not pinned or reviewed here. None was built or tested.
  Left out: libopenh264. Its licence and patent position were not established for this build.
  Never: libx264, libx265 or any GPL or nonfree component.

--enable-small
  It selects size optimisation (optflags=$cflags_size) and defines CONFIG_SMALL 1. No codec,
  filter, muxer or demuxer is switched off by it: allcodecs.c, allfilters.c, allformats.c and
  the library Makefiles do not gate any component on CONFIG_SMALL (only the table generators'
  host flags). Its effects are smaller, slower code paths (869 source files test CONFIG_SMALL),
  no Windows version resource (configure skips windres), and dropped descriptive strings:
  NULL_IF_CONFIG_SMALL makes -filters print "(null)" descriptions and -encoders/-decoders
  print empty long names. This was read from the source, not measured against a build without
  the flag.

  FriBidi 1.0.16      LGPL-2.1-or-later   third-party/FriBidi-COPYING.txt
  HarfBuzz 10.1.0     MIT-Modern-Variant  third-party/HarfBuzz-COPYING.txt

  zimg 3.0.5          WTFPL               third-party/zimg-COPYING.txt
  zlib 1.3.2          Zlib                third-party/zlib-LICENSE.txt

  LicenseRef-MinGW-w64-runtime AND MIT AND BSD-3-Clause AND GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1
  (ffprobe: LGPL-2.1-or-later AND the four toolchain runtime terms)
Toolchain runtime, linked statically by `-static -static-libgcc` (notices shipped with the binary):
  mingw-w64 C runtime (crt 14.0.0.r426)  third-party/MinGW-w64-runtime-COPYING.txt
                                         (its text requires the notices with binaries)
  winpthreads 14.0.0.r426                third-party/winpthreads-COPYING.txt (MIT and BSD-style)
  libgcc, libstdc++ (GCC 16.2.0)         third-party/GCC-RUNTIME-LIBRARY-EXCEPTION.txt
                                         (GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1)
  Observed with nm on the unstripped local builds: both exes hold winpthreads symbols (123
  pthread_*) and libgcc's ___chkstk_ms; the export ffmpeg also holds libstdc++ (434 std
  symbols, 21 __cxa_/__gxx_), the decode ffprobe holds none. The three texts are copied from
  the toolchain packages (mingw-w64-x86_64-crt, -winpthreads, -gcc-libs) by the recipe.
  The catalog rows list them as the toolchain runtime components mingw-w64-runtime,
  winpthreads and gcc-runtime (libgcc.a and libstdc++.a ship in the gcc package), pinned by
  the MSYS2 package files of the CI runner that built the catalog binary (windows-2025, run
  38137274090, <name>.evidence/toolchain-packages.txt):
    mingw-w64-x86_64-crt-14.0.0.r426.g4564ee4b5-1-any.pkg.tar.zst
      5513117e204c933ed3b3e17b1bb809667653b72b3ca932d0c048ffc8f01f3801
    mingw-w64-x86_64-winpthreads-14.0.0.r426.g4564ee4b5-1-any.pkg.tar.zst
      f8e8cea030192fedc17a41167a868c4de909ebf01ea9730d8d1133641b208785
    mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc-16.2.0-4-any.pkg.tar.zst
      7928a168fe0827e6ba41ea672a9957a5bfa47f732f6922e86cf0f24dd61e5d0c
  (digests from pacman's sync database entries for exactly the installed versions; the runner
  keeps no package files). Also on the runner: binutils 2.47-3, headers 14.0.0.r426.g4564ee4b5-1.
  The local validation toolchain was older (crt and winpthreads 14.0.0.r98.g19f5121a2-1,
  gcc 16.1.0-5), so its binaries differ from the CI ones.

CI builds (ffmpeg-windows workflow, windows-2025)
  ffmpeg, export-ass-zimg: runs 38132992466, 38134157839 and 38137274090 all gave
    sha256 2ecd3ab3d313f1a09ad29491979f806faf98c38d150ab37ec2978627fcb9cdb9, 19496448 bytes.
    -version reports "built with gcc 16.2.0 (Rev4, Built by MSYS2 project)".
  The recipe sets SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 so strip writes no timestamp into the PE header.
  The approved Windows decode build (BUILD-NOTES.txt) links the same runtime the same way; its
  catalog row now lists the same three notice files.
LGPL obligations: FFmpeg and FriBidi are statically linked into one executable; ship the
notices plus a written source offer covering their complete sources and this recipe.

To reproduce (MSYS2 MINGW64 shell, from rightkit/crates/rightkit-media):
  recipes/build-ffmpeg-windows.sh fetch --variant export-ass-zimg --sources <src-dir>
  PYTHON=<venv>/Scripts/python.exe MESON=<venv>/Scripts/meson.exe NINJA=<venv>/Scripts/ninja.exe \
    PKG_CONFIG=<venv>/Lib/site-packages/pkgconf/.bin/pkgconf.exe \
    recipes/build-ffmpeg-windows.sh build --variant export-ass-zimg --tool ffmpeg \
    --sources <src-dir> --work <work-dir> --out <out-dir>
  recipes/build-ffmpeg-windows.sh build --variant decode --tool ffprobe ... (PYTHON only)
or dispatch the ffmpeg-windows workflow with variant and tool.
